Measure and characterize the transient structure (such as temperature and species distribution) of diffusion flames established at initially non-steady, spherical flame structures for mixtures of different H2/CH4/diluent ratios   (soot-free) and different C2H4/diluent ratios (sooty), for different flow rates.

objective_summary.value: The investigation aims to study spherical diffusion flames of soot-free and sooty gaseous fuel mixtures in microgravity to measure flame structure, extinction limits, and pulsating instabilities. These experimental data are used to compare with and validate detailed computational chemical kinetics and transport models.

earth_applications.value: Understanding diffusion flame dynamics and chemistry supports improving the performance, power, efficiency, reliability, and pollutant emissions of combustion engines and devices on Earth.
earth_applications.quote: Practically, with diffusion flame burning as the basis in many combustion engines and devices, understanding the underlying dynamics and chemistry of diffusion flames is important in improving performance in terms of power, efficiency, pollutant emissions, and reliability.
